features.title: Arena and bot catalogs
features.requirement: Load arena and bot definitions, classify ordinary and special arenas, preserve four-arena tier ordering and launch the selected map with its authored opponents.

evidence.observation: Loads base and listed arena definitions and assigns single-player, special and other arena numbers.
The original classifies single-player arenas and truncates incomplete tiers.

workflows.trigger: Open single-player with stock and additional arena definitions mounted.
steps: Inspect tier ordering, training and final selections.
Launch an arena and compare map, bots and selected difficulty with its definition.
workflows.observableOutcome: Every valid catalog choice reaches its authored map and opponents; ignored definitions have a diagnostic.

features.title: Difficulty-specific arena records
features.requirement: Retain best finishing rank independently for all five skills, prefer the highest skill for equal best ranks, and persist records across application restarts.

evidence.observation: Writes only improved ranks to the selected g_spScores skill record.
Scans five skill records and retains the higher skill on equal rank.
Source accepts ranks one through eight and refuses worse results.

workflows.trigger: Finish the same arena at several ranks and skill settings.
steps: Earn an improved result, a worse result and an equal rank at a higher skill.
Restart and reopen the arena selection.
workflows.observableOutcome: The best rank and skill remain correct and worse results do not erase progress.

features.title: Persistent medals and award thresholds
features.requirement: Accumulate accuracy, impressive, excellent, gauntlet, frag and perfect awards with source thresholds and show their earned values in postgame and progression UI.

evidence.observation: Adds award values to persistent g_spAwards entries.
Postgame calculates accuracy and hundred-frag thresholds and presents earned awards.
Original accumulates award counters rather than replacing them.

workflows.trigger: Complete matches that cross accuracy and hundred-frag award thresholds.
steps: Earn repeated awards and finish a perfect match.
Reopen postgame and restart the application.
workflows.observableOutcome: Counts accumulate once per reported result and medal displays survive restart.

gaps: Complete bot-driven progression and award presentation still require live acceptance; source inspection is not a passing game session.

features.title: Tier completion and movie unlocks
features.requirement: Unlock tiers and tier movies according to completed arena wins, preserve training and final special cases, and retain one-time completion flags and replay availability.

evidence.observation: Requires first-place records for every ordinary arena in a tier.
Persists the tier video flag and reports first-time availability.
Defines four-arena completion and training/final handling.

workflows.trigger: Win the last unfinished arena in a tier.
steps: Verify a partial tier remains unfinished.
Complete the tier, view or skip its movie, restart and replay the unlocked movie.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only the qualifying win unlocks progression; movies remain replayable without awarding the tier twice.

features.title: Progression reset and explicit unlock commands
features.requirement: Expose the authored reset confirmation and developer unlock commands, clearing scores, awards and videos only after reset is accepted and preserving the separate unlock-all and medal-unlock behaviors.

evidence.observation: Resets single-player score, award and video cvars.
Cancel returns without clearing progress; accept resets the game and selection.
Original explicit command marks tiers and arenas unlocked.
Original medal command sets award values separately.

workflows.trigger: Choose reset with existing progress, then invoke each explicit unlock command in an authorized developer session.
steps: Cancel reset and verify records remain.
Accept reset, restart, then compare each unlock command with the original.
workflows.observableOutcome: Reset and unlock operations have distinct, durable effects and do not silently overwrite one another.

features.title: Podium, postgame and next-match navigation
features.requirement: Present ranked players, ties, award sequencing, winner announcements and music, and route next, replay and menu actions according to the arena result.

evidence.observation: Owns result parsing, award phases, winner sound and next/replay focus.
Original constructs the postgame state from match results.

workflows.trigger: End an arena with a win, loss and tied displayed rank.
steps: Observe podium and award phases.
Choose replay, next and return-to-menu in separate runs.
workflows.observableOutcome: Visible places, announcements and selected next map match the actual completed result.

features.title: Team Arena skirmish scores and best times
features.requirement: Preserve per-map and mode postgame records, time and shutout bonuses, skill multiplier, winning high-score rules, demo availability and restoration of pre-skirmish settings.

evidence.observation: Computes bonuses, writes a winning improved score and restores saved settings.
Defines Team Arena score computation and postgame persistence.

workflows.trigger: Finish a Team Arena skirmish faster than the target time.
steps: Compare winning, losing and shutout results at several skills.
Reload the record and start a normal server session.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only qualifying high scores replace the saved record and temporary skirmish settings are restored.

features.title: Free-for-all deathmatch
features.requirement: Run free-for-all with independent player scores, authored death and suicide penalties, spawn rules, frag/time limits and sudden death on tied scores.

evidence.observation: Checks team and individual limits and defers exit while scores are tied.
Original orders tie, time, player-count, frag and capture checks.

workflows.trigger: Launch free-for-all with a short frag limit and time limit.
steps: Score frags and a suicide.
Reach a tied limit, break the tie and complete intermission.
workflows.observableOutcome: The correct player wins only after the tie resolves and the scoreboard agrees with score events.

features.title: Tournament duel and spectator queue
features.requirement: Keep two active duelists, ordered spectator admission, winner/loser records, loser rotation and map restart behavior.

evidence.observation: Selects the eligible waiting spectator for an open duelist slot.
Updates winner and loser session records.
Original admits the longest-waiting eligible spectator.

workflows.trigger: Join a tournament with three players and one spectator.
steps: Finish a duel and observe loser removal.
Disconnect an active player and inspect the next admission.
workflows.observableOutcome: Exactly two players compete and queue order, wins and losses survive the round transition.

features.title: Single-player arena match flow
features.requirement: Run the single-player game type with authored bot roster, result delivery, intermission handling and return to progression UI.

evidence.observation: Loads arena definitions and populates the single-player roster.
Publishes results and moves clients into intermission.
Original loads bots and authored single-player opponents.

workflows.trigger: Select an ordinary or special single-player arena.
steps: Play through a real bot match to its score limit.
Continue from the resulting postgame screen.
workflows.observableOutcome: The selected opponents actually participate and the completed result reaches the correct progression record.

gaps: A full bot-driven training-to-final campaign remains an acceptance obligation.

features.title: Team deathmatch scoring and spawns
features.requirement: Preserve team assignment, team scoring, friendly-fire settings, balancing, player spawns and team-based limits.

evidence.observation: Updates team scores and lead/tie announcements.
Determines team relationships only for applicable game types.
Original emits tied, lead and scored team events.

workflows.trigger: Host team deathmatch with both teams and configurable friendly fire.
steps: Score against enemies and teammates under each setting.
Change teams and reach the team frag limit.
workflows.observableOutcome: Team totals, damage policy, player placement and winning announcement agree with selected rules.

features.title: Two-flag CTF
features.requirement: Preserve pickup, carried and dropped flags, own-flag return, capture conditions, timeout return, carrier-defense bonuses, assists and product-specific scoring.

evidence.observation: Handles recovery, capture, assist windows and base-versus-missionpack bonuses.
Awards carrier and base-defense events.
Original requires the enemy flag and handles dropped own-flag recovery separately.

workflows.trigger: Start CTF with both team bases and flag entities.
steps: Steal, drop, return and time out flags.
Capture with and without the own flag at base and within assist windows.
workflows.observableOutcome: Flag state, capture score, assists and announcements match the selected product for every transition.

features.title: Team Arena One Flag CTF

evidence.observation: Routes neutral flag pickup and opposing-base delivery for GT_1FCTF.

workflows.trigger: Launch One Flag CTF with a neutral flag and both team bases.
steps: Try delivery at the own base, then the opposing base.
Kill the carrier and exercise recovery and timeout paths.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only valid opposing-base delivery scores and every client sees the same neutral-flag state.

features.title: Team Arena Overload obelisks
features.requirement: Preserve obelisk health, enemy-only damage, attack warnings, regeneration, destruction score, presentation state and delayed respawn.

evidence.observation: Scores destruction and schedules obelisk respawn.
Regenerates health and updates the model health indicator.

workflows.trigger: Damage an enemy obelisk in Overload.
steps: Attempt friendly damage and allow partial damage to regenerate.
Destroy the obelisk and wait for its configured respawn.
workflows.observableOutcome: Health, warning cadence, team score and respawn timing agree across server, HUD and world model.

features.title: Team Arena Harvester skulls
features.requirement: Generate death cubes at the neutral obelisk, collect opposing-team cubes, carry counts, expire uncollected cubes and deliver skulls at the enemy obelisk for score.

evidence.observation: Creates team-colored cubes at the neutral obelisk after deaths.
Delivers carried skulls, awards score and clears the carried count.
Original validates opposing base and converts carried tokens to score.

workflows.trigger: Kill opponents in Harvester and visit the neutral obelisk.
steps: Compare own-team and enemy-team cube pickups and timeout.
Carry multiple skulls to each base and die while carrying.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only eligible skulls increase the carried count and valid delivery scores exactly that count once.

features.title: Warmup, readiness, sudden death and rotation
features.requirement: Preserve required-player warmup, countdown restarts, tied-score sudden death, intermission minimum/timeout and ready rules, nextmap rotation and map_restart.

evidence.observation: Waits for required players and starts or restarts warmup.
Combines human readiness with intermission timing.

workflows.trigger: Start a match below its required player count.
steps: Join and leave during warmup, then complete a tied match.
Vary human readiness during intermission and inspect the next map.
workflows.observableOutcome: Gameplay, result publication and rotation occur at the authored conditions without losing connected players.

features.title: Quake 3 weapons and projectile behavior
features.requirement: Preserve gauntlet, machinegun, shotgun, grenade launcher, rocket launcher, lightning gun, railgun, plasma gun, BFG and authored grapple behavior, including spread, range, splash, ammo and firing cadence.

Exercise ricochet, projectile lifetime and grapple attach/release.
workflows.observableOutcome: Weapon state, damage and visible impacts match original behavior under the selected Q3 movement and combat profiles.

features.title: Damage, armor, knockback and death lifecycle
features.requirement: Preserve armor absorption, damage flags, friendly-fire policy, knockback, protection, corpse/gib state, drops, respawn and score attribution.

workflows.observableOutcome: One authoritative damage result controls health, armor, impulse, death events and credited score.

features.title: Inventory, timed powerups and item lifecycle
features.requirement: Preserve pickup eligibility, quantities, ammo/health/armor caps, timed powerup extension, holdable ownership, dropped items, respawn delays and item-team selection.

evidence.observation: Dispatches ammo, weapon, health, armor, powerup, holdable and team pickups.

features.title: Team Arena nailgun and chaingun
features.requirement: Preserve the nailgun projectile fan, nail speeds and spread, chaingun hitscan spread and cadence, expansion ammo and accuracy accounting.

MISSIONPACK weapon branches and accuracy-shot counting.

steps: Count nail projectiles and chaingun hit events.
Compare ammo, accuracy counters and damage across repeated seeded shots.
workflows.observableOutcome: Expansion projectiles and hitscan effects preserve their distinct source behavior and cannot collapse into a base weapon.

features.title: Proximity mine arming, attachment and detonation
features.requirement: Preserve mine flight, surface attachment, delayed arming, team-aware trigger radius, shootability, lifetime, player attachment, stacked mines and invulnerability interactions.

evidence.observation: Constructs the proximity missile with its product behavior.
Routes proximity contact to surface or player handling.
Original handles attached and stacked player mines.
Original arms triggers and mine health after attachment.

workflows.trigger: Launch mines onto geometry and players.
steps: Enter the trigger radius before and after arming with teammates and enemies.
Stack player mines, shoot an armed mine and wait for timeout.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only valid triggers detonate and attached, timed and destroyed mines release their owned entities correctly.

features.title: Guard, Scout, Doubler and Ammo Regen
features.requirement: Preserve persistent powerup acquisition and exclusive ownership, Guard health/armor and regeneration, Scout movement/armor rules, Doubler damage, Ammo Regen timing, and death drops.

evidence.observation: Applies handicap-derived Guard/Scout stats and Ammo Regen timers.
Restores the owned persistent powerup on death.

workflows.trigger: Acquire each persistent powerup in a Team Arena match.
steps: Measure its movement, damage, health, armor and ammo effects.
Attempt replacement, die, respawn and pick the dropped powerup back up.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only the active powerup affects the player and ownership transitions preserve the correct world pickup and timers.

features.title: Holdables, kamikaze and invulnerability
features.requirement: Preserve medkit and teleporter use, kamikaze activation and death-triggered waves, invulnerability duration, collision sphere and projectile reflection, with authored consumption and event timing.

evidence.observation: Dispatches source holdable events into game behavior.
Creates the kamikaze damage-wave entity.
Calculates the invulnerability impact position and reflection response.
Original creates the timed kamikaze controller.

workflows.trigger: Acquire and use each product-appropriate holdable.
steps: Activate medkit/teleporter while injured or carrying objectives.
Exercise kamikaze waves and invulnerability against hitscan and projectiles.
workflows.observableOutcome: Each holdable consumes and expires correctly; effects, damage and protection follow the selected product rules.

features.title: Team Arena personal portals
features.requirement: Place a portal destination and source, preserve enable and lifetime delays, teleport eligible players, handle missing/destroyed destinations and drop carried flags according to source.

evidence.observation: Drops carried flags and resolves the linked destination before teleport.
Creates the source portal and its delayed activation.
Original pairs portal source with its destination identifier.

workflows.trigger: Use a personal teleporter to place both portal endpoints.
steps: Touch before and after activation while carrying a flag.
Destroy or expire the destination and touch the remaining source.
workflows.observableOutcome: Portal timing, destination, objective drops and failure behavior match the authored rules.

features.title: Bot catalog, skill, delayed spawn and population
features.requirement: Load bot definitions and personalities, accept skill/team/name choices, queue delayed spawns, remove bots, and maintain bot_minplayers without displacing human participation.

evidence.observation: Counts humans and bots and adds or removes bots for population targets.
Begins due delayed bot spawns.
Original population management treats teams and spectators explicitly.

workflows.trigger: Host a populated server with bot_minplayers enabled.
steps: Add named bots with several skills and delayed starts.
Join and leave as humans and change the population target.
workflows.observableOutcome: Actual connected bot counts, teams, identities and spawn times match the requested configuration.

features.title: Bot personality, skill interpolation and chat
features.requirement: Preserve character characteristics, skill interpolation, chat scripts, event-driven responses, synonym matching and chat timing without replacing individual personalities with one generic bot.

evidence.observation: Owns loaded character data and skill-dependent characteristic lookup.
Selects authored enter-game chat behavior.
Original loads/interpolates bot character settings.
Original personality and context decide enter-game chat.

workflows.trigger: Spawn several named personalities at different skills.
steps: Trigger entry, death, kill and conversational events.
Compare aim/movement characteristic inputs and emitted chat timing.
workflows.observableOutcome: Bot personalities and skill levels produce their authored characteristics and eligible contextual responses.

features.title: Bot goals, combat choices and movement execution
features.requirement: Preserve item weights, long/near-term goals, weapon weights, combat aiming, retreat, obstacle handling and travel maneuvers through actual bot user commands.

evidence.observation: Selects long-term item goals with inventory and travel flags.
Chooses a weapon using the configured inventory weights.
Executes movement toward a goal through route and travel handling.
Original movement handles reachability, blocked movement and special travel.

workflows.trigger: Run a bot through combat with scarce health, ammo and several routes.
steps: Observe item/weapon decisions and execute jumps, elevators and teleport travel.
Block a route, injure the bot and repeat after death/respawn.
workflows.observableOutcome: Bots actually acquire goals, fight and recover movement using the source behavior rather than only returning valid route data.

features.title: AAS world loading and route queries
features.requirement: Load map-matched AAS with BSP spatial data, preserve areas, presence types, travel flags, cached route costs, alternative routes and dynamic area enable state.

evidence.observation: Attaches botlib to the active server map, BSP and spatial host.
Evaluates source routing costs for an area and goal.
Original routes with allowed travel flags and area costs.

steps: Compare source and unified routes under different presence and travel restrictions.
Disable a traversed area and reload the map.
workflows.observableOutcome: Route reachability and travel costs reflect the current world and never reuse stale data from another map.

features.title: AAS reachability, clustering, writing and optimization
features.requirement: Preserve runtime reachability generation, special travel links, cluster/portal formation, optimized AAS output and read-back behavior as distinct navigation operations.

evidence.observation: Processes area reachability and special travel during AAS initialization.
Builds and validates AAS clusters and portals.
Original advances reachability construction.

workflows.trigger: Initialize an AAS world that requires regenerated reachability or clustering.
steps: Build routes through jumps, ladders, launch pads and movers.
Write and reload optimized navigation and compare route results.
workflows.observableOutcome: Regenerated and reloaded navigation retains the source connectivity and costs.

gaps: Existing reachability, cluster and writer code does not construct a navigation world directly from every required map format.

features.title: Navigation construction for foreign maps and moving geometry
features.requirement: Construct usable navigation from every required Q1, Q2 and Q3 map geometry profile, preserve hull/presence constraints and moving-geometry links, and prove bots can complete routes and objectives without preexisting AAS.

evidence.observation: Original BSPC constructs navigation geometry, areas and settings from the loaded BSP tree.
BSPC map/brush construction and command-line workflows remain unported despite runtime AAS support.

workflows.trigger: Load an authored foreign map with no compatible navigation file.
steps: Construct navigation from the actual collision world.
Run bots through doors, platforms, teleports and the selected objective on that map.
workflows.observableOutcome: Bots navigate and finish objectives using generated data whose provenance identifies the exact geometry and behavior profile.

gaps: No complete TypeScript BSPC map/brush construction donor exists.
Moving geometry and cross-game actor hulls require explicit construction and live traversal evidence.

features.title: CTF team orders for all flag states
features.requirement: Preserve offensive/defensive assignment for both flags at base, own missing, enemy missing and both missing, including carrier escort, return requests, strategy, roster size and travel-time ordering.

evidence.observation: Dispatches all four flag-state order branches.
Assigns return, escort and attack roles for both missing flags.

steps: Run small and large rosters with aggressive and defensive strategy.
Observe issued commands and follow the assigned bots through their actual tasks.
workflows.observableOutcome: Assignments and executed goals match the correct flag-state branch, including carrier support.

gaps: The complete executed flag-state, roster-size and strategy matrix has not been demonstrated.

features.title: One Flag team orders and carrier response
features.requirement: Preserve order selection while the flag is at center, held by either team or dropped, including escort, intercept, return and attack transitions.

evidence.observation: Dispatches neutral-flag team order branches.
Selects executed One Flag goals from current possession state.
Original One Flag status dispatch.

workflows.trigger: Move the neutral flag through center, friendly carrier, enemy carrier and dropped states.
steps: Repeat with a human and bot carrier.
Kill or disconnect the carrier and inspect reassignment.
workflows.observableOutcome: Team orders drive actual escort/interception and update when flag possession changes.

gaps: Uncommon neutral-flag order and execution combinations still require original-versus-unified runtime evidence.

features.title: Overload and Harvester team coordination
features.requirement: Preserve source attack/defend splits for Overload and harvest/defend splits for Harvester, including carried-cube goals, aggression and task preferences.

Chooses harvest orders through the shared team split.
Selects harvest or delivery goals based on carried cubes.

steps: Vary team size, aggression and task preferences.
Follow bots through base attacks, cube collection and skull delivery.
workflows.observableOutcome: Bots execute the correct mode objective and retain source role allocation as team state changes.

gaps: A shared order helper does not prove both objective modes complete their actions; live mode-specific coverage remains required.

features.title: Human leadership, subteams and task preferences
features.requirement: Preserve human/bot leader selection, leader start/stop requests, absence recovery, subteam membership and offense/defense preferences in assignment order.

evidence.observation: Recognizes active human team leadership.
Orders eligible teammates by their task preference.
Handles the text subteam request.

steps: Issue preferences and subteam changes.
Disconnect or relinquish leadership during an objective change.
workflows.observableOutcome: Eligible leadership and preference changes affect subsequent commands and task execution without stale client references.

features.title: Text orders, patrols, acknowledgements and refusals
features.requirement: Parse addressed team commands for help, accompany, defend, camp, patrol, item pickup, flag return, attack and harvest; preserve durations, waypoint loops, acknowledgement and refusal rules.

evidence.observation: Builds patrol waypoint sequences from matched command text.
Resolves the addressed bot and requested accompany/help task.
Emits the authored refusal behavior.
Original installs patrol goals and ordering state.

steps: Issue valid, expired, ambiguous and unreachable orders.
Observe replies and execute the requested movement or objective.
workflows.observableOutcome: Only addressed eligible bots accept orders, retain their durations and waypoints, and acknowledge or refuse according to source.

features.title: Voice commands, team responses and taunts
features.requirement: Preserve team-scoped voice command routing, source command vocabulary, leadership and task messages, acknowledgements and event-selected taunts.

evidence.observation: Parses voice command speaker and dispatches the authored command vocabulary.
Resolves the current friendly carrier for follow orders.
Original voice dispatcher verifies team context and named handlers.

workflows.trigger: Send voice orders from teammates, opponents and spectators.
steps: Request getflag, defend, follow, return and leadership actions.
Trigger and inspect taunts after gameplay events.
workflows.observableOutcome: Eligible recipients hear the right voice and perform its task; unrelated teams do not inherit the order.

features.title: Team changes and spectator following
features.requirement: Preserve team admission and balancing, spectator modes, follow by client/name, forward/backward follow cycling and reset of followed state after disconnect or team change.

evidence.observation: Handles team requests, balance and spectator state transitions.
Selects an eligible next or previous player to follow.

steps: Cycle targets in both directions.
Disconnect the followed player and attempt disallowed team changes.
workflows.observableOutcome: Spectator view and team membership always reference an eligible player and respect the selected admission rules.

features.title: Player identity, chat and scoreboards
features.requirement: Preserve names, colors, model/skin and handicap settings, scoreboard columns and rank order, public/team/private text delivery, voice messages and spectator restrictions.

evidence.observation: Formats and routes public, team and direct chat.
Publishes player score, ping, awards and team data.
Owns editable player identity and handicap controls.
Original chat recipient and text formatting rules.

steps: Send public, team and private text and voice messages.
Open scoreboards before and after score or team changes.
workflows.observableOutcome: Each recipient sees only eligible messages and the scoreboard identifies the correct players and current results.

features.requirement: Preserve status, map/restart, kick, serverinfo/systeminfo, IP filters, command logging, rcon authentication and flood limits, with a usable interactive dedicated console.

features.title: Connection challenge, admission and reconnect

features.requirement: Preserve packet sequence handling, qport routing, fragment assembly, duplicate/out-of-order rejection, reliable command acknowledgements and overflow behavior.

features.requirement: Preserve gamestate/baselines, visibility-selected entity snapshots, playerstate deltas, command replay, prediction error correction, interpolation and event deduplication.
